strengths: Well-motivated contribution addressing genuine gap in predictive coding literature; brain employs both generative and discriminative inference
Elegant theoretical framework: unified energy function (Eq. 3) naturally combines genPC and discPC rather than using ad-hoc approaches
Maintains biological plausibility with local computations and Hebbian learning rules throughout; clear neural circuit implementation
Comprehensive experimental evaluation across multiple datasets, learning settings, and architectures with rigorous baselines and statistical reporting
Strong empirical results: bPC consistently matches/exceeds unidirectional models in their domains and outperforms hybridPC across tasks
Insightful energy landscape analysis (Section 4.4) providing clear intuition for why bPC works—sharpening discriminative minima while anchoring to data via generative feedback
Exemplary reproducibility: extensive supplementary material with detailed hyperparameters, architectural specifications, ablations, and promised code release
Demonstrates effectiveness on biologically-relevant tasks (multimodal learning, inference with missing information) showing practical relevance beyond standard classification
weaknesses: Limited algorithmic novelty: core contribution of combining two energy functions is conceptually straightforward; lacks deeper theoretical insight into why this combination is optimal

Hyperparameter tuning burden undermines unified framework narrative: αgen and αdisc require task-specific tuning with significant sensitivity (Appendix D); different settings for supervised vs. unsupervised learning; no learnable scaling implemented

Computational cost largely unaddressed: missing information inference requires 600,000 steps (MNIST) or 3,000 (deep models); no timing comparisons provided; two-stage inference for deep models suggests convergence difficulties
Inconsistent performance on complex tasks: bPC achieves 85.06% on CIFAR-10 combined task vs. hybridBP's 90.11% (Table 14); reconstruction RMSE gaps remain relative to BP methods
Limited architectural scope: only VGG tested for deep models; no ResNets, modern optimizers, or ImageNet evaluation; max-pooling incompatibility requires workarounds limiting architectural choices

Biological plausibility claims need tempering: separate error neurons assumption is neurobiologically debatable; brain connection is motivational rather than validational; claims about resembling biological inference not firmly supported
Energy landscape analysis limited to toy XOR problem; unclear how insights generalize to high-dimensional spaces; real-task landscapes would be more convincing

Incomplete baseline comparisons: mentions U-Nets, VAEVAE, VAR, PredNet in related work but provides no experimental comparisons; limited comparison with other biologically plausible learning algorithms
Dense presentation with critical experimental details relegated to appendices; some choices (specific inference step counts, initialization schemes) lack justification in main text
Missing practical guidance: no decision framework for when to use bPC vs. alternatives; scalability to modern architectures undemonstrated; convergence analysis lacking
